title: cost-optimization: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost for common production workloads by automating sensible defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching, surfacing quantization profiles, and providing a simple unit-economics (UEcon) view and suggested actions. This PR wires together three complementary subsystems: (1) an autotune service that observes traffic and recommends batching/caching defaults per-route and per-model; (2) quantization profile support in the model registry with heuristics and safe fallbacks; (3) a UEcon tooling dashboard + API endpoint that shows estimated cost-per-call, token efficiency, and automated suggestions. Changes include infra, runtime, API, docs and console integration. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] end-to-end bench runs for representative workloads - [x] console UI hook + e2e smoke - [x] feature-flagged rollout plan Summary of changes: - Add autotune service (internal microservice) that aggregates request/latency/cost samples and produces per-route recommendations (batch size, max latency SLO target for batching, cache prefixes to enable). - Extend routing/runtime config schema to accept recommended defaults and to support 'autotune_source: service' with confidence scores. - Add quantization_profile objects to model registry: recommended quant settings, expected perf/cost delta, and safe fallback chain (FP16 -> int8 -> int4). - UEcon API: new /v1/uecon/estimate endpoint and background job that computes estimated cost-per-call using runtime profiles, kernel-cost coefficients, and recent traffic distribution. - Console integration: new UEcon panel with suggested actions (apply recommendation, test canary) and projected savings. - Tests: unit tests for policy selection, integration tests against local runtime, and benchmark harness adding three representative workloads. Migration and backwards compatibility: recommendations are inert until applied; new registry fields are optional and default to prior behavior. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout with canary (5% traffic) for two weeks, gated by no >2% error increase and stable latency. Follow-ups: add automated apply-schedule (maintenance window), improve confidence calibration using A/B results, and surface bucketing by customer tier.
